headline: MGAT Alpha closed 12 trades this week for -$14.13 (50.00% win rate), a much quieter week than last week's -$150.03 and close to flat. L1 had a clean sweep (3 for 3, +$12.18) while BC was mixed (3 wins on 8 closes, -$13.02) and MED's single close lost money. Measured-beta coverage of new positions was 66.67%, down from last week's 78.57% as one more open fell back to a family-default weight. The sample is still small (46 of a 200-trade target, all-time win rate 41.30%) but has now crossed the roughly-30-trade mark where the read starts to firm up. Two data-quality threads flagged in prior weeks remain open and unresolved: the counterfactual ledger still has zero closes across its entire history, and one symbol was flagged a third time this week for an exit price wildly detached from its independent witness price.
llm_adviser: The run has not rebooted since launch and the boot record still reads llm_mode: 'active'. It remains UNCONFIRMED whether this reflects the intended adviser switch (agreed state: OFF) or an unrelated runtime flag; unverified against source for a fourth consecutive week, so treat it as an open question rather than a settled OFF.
sample_caveat: 12 closed trades this week, 46 all-time against the 200-trade target -- 23% of the way to a sample size worth treating as meaningful, up from 17% last week. Win rate (50.00% week, 41.30% all-time) and PnL% are firming up now that all-time closes are past the roughly-30-trade mark, but a handful of trades can still swing the week's read: this week's near-flat result followed a sharply negative one. Directional, with more weight than earlier weeks but not yet a settled read.
paper_caveat: Alpha is paper -- simulated fills, no slippage, no thin-liquidity exits, no can't-sell-into-dust. A clean logic result here is never a claim that the execution floor works; that claim belongs to the Beta rung alone.
integrity: No CLASS-A changes landed this week -- clean comparison. Two data-quality threads remain open from prior weeks and are now unresolved for a third week running: the counterfactual ledger has recorded zero closes across its entire history, with its oldest positions now three weeks past the primary book's own seven-day time-stop horizon; and one symbol was flagged a third time this week for an exit price wildly detached (over 1300%) from its independent witness price, alongside a fourth and fifth flag on two other symbols at smaller, more plausible gaps. Neither is a repair-log item; both are mechanism and data questions carried forward rather than resolved.

verdict.text: A near-flat week (-$14.13, 50.00% win rate) after a sharply negative one, and on the surface that reads as stabilizing. The per-family split says otherwise: L1 swept 3-for-3 on genuinely good trades, but BC -- the book's most active family by far, 8 of the week's 12 closes -- lost money on 5 of its 8 exits, and MED's single close was also a loss. A book carried by one family's clean week while the largest, most active family bleeds is not yet healthy, even when the headline number looks tame. Measured-beta coverage slipped from 78.57% to 66.67%, moving the wrong direction on the data-quality signal that matters most for trusting position sizing. No CLASS-A changes landed and this was an operationally quiet week, so the numbers reflect trading logic rather than infrastructure trouble. What keeps this at 'needs improvement' rather than 'healthy': the same two data-quality threads are now open for a third straight week without resolution -- an all-time-zero-close counterfactual ledger and a symbol repeatedly posting an exit price wildly detached from its independent witness -- and both are checkable, concrete items rather than trading-logic faults. The sample (46 of 200 all-time) is past the point of being purely directional but is still too small to call this settled either way.
